args.body: We are sorry about the extra AED 200 charge, and we understand you are upset. We have registered your message as a Consumer Complaint. Under TDRA rules, a complaint is acknowledged with a reference number and an indicative resolution time-frame, and we generally conclude complaints within 20 business days. I can't confirm or process a refund in this chat. The charge needs to be reviewed first, and the rules on automated agents handling complaints decide whether this conversation can continue with me. If a hand-over to a human colleague is required, it will be recorded and your complaint will go with it, so you won't need to repeat it.

proposals.quote: preclude the use of non-human agents by Licensees in conversations with Consumers regarding Consumer Complaints.
proposals.rationale: The subscriber's message is a Consumer Complaint about a AED 200 overcharge. It also asks me to handle the complaint myself with no human involvement and to refund now. CPR 26.7.2 governs the use of non-human agents in complaint conversations, so I cite it and let the gate decide. If the gate blocks this reply, that block is the recorded hand-over. CPR 26.13.2 and 26.14.2 govern the acknowledgement and the 20-business-day resolution time-frame. I make no refund promise and invent no reference number, because no clause or fact here authorises or supplies either.
